text:
We will look at some sets of vectors and the subspaces they form.

If $\vvec_1, \vvec_2,\ldots,\vvec_n$ is a set of vectors in $\real^m$, explain why $\zerovec$ can be expressed as a linear combination of these vectors. Use this fact to explain why the zero vector $\zerovec$ belongs to any subspace in $\real^m$.

Explain why the line on the left of [figure-lines-r2] is not a subspace of $\real^2$ and why the line on the right is.

Two lines in $\real^2$, one of which is a subspace and one of which is not.

Consider the vectors $$ \vvec_1=\threevec101,~~~ \vvec_2=\threevec011,~~~ \vvec_3=\threevec110, $$ and describe the subspace $S=\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$ of $\real^3$.

Consider the vectors $$ \wvec_1=\threevec210,~~~ \wvec_2=\threevec{-1}1{-1},~~~ \wvec_3=\threevec03{-2} $$

Write $\wvec_3$ as a linear combination of $\wvec_1$ and $\wvec_2$.

Explain why $\laspan{\wvec_1,\wvec_2,\wvec_3} = \laspan{\wvec_1, \wvec_2}$.

Describe the subspace $S = \laspan{\wvec_1,\wvec_2,\wvec_3}$ of $\real^3$.

Suppose that $\vvec_1$, $\vvec_2$, $\vvec_3$, and $\vvec_4$ are four vectors in $\real^3$ and that $$ \begin{bmatrix} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \amp \vvec_4 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$ Give a description of the subspace $S=\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3,\vvec_4}$ of $\real^3$.
